title: Short Gut Syndrome in the NICU: Explained | Cincinnati Children's

sentences.text: MUSIC PLAYING] My name is Kara McNealis, and I am a neonatologist at Cincinnati Children's. And my name is Jackie Wessel, and I am a dietitian at Cincinnati Children's. We are here today to talk about short gut syndrome in the newborn intensive care unit.
Short gut syndrome is a problem with not having enough bowel, and this can be present from birth or develop after an infant needs surgery.
Some of the problems that may be present at birth that can lead to short gut syndrome are vovulus or intestinal atresia.
Short gut syndrome can develop after a baby is born, like when an infant needs surgery for necrotizing and taro colitis.
Infants with short gut syndrome need very careful management of their nutrition.
Because they do not have a normal length of bowel, they need IV nutrition called parenteral nutrition or TPN.
Parenteral nutrition is delivered via an IV.
So infants will have a central line, which is a deep IV that is stable and in place for a long time.
When it is safe, we provide a small volume of milk to infants with short gut syndrome.
This helps stimulate the bowel to remodel and absorb better.
It is important to go very slowly on milk feedings to protect the remaining bowel.
Breast milk is very important for protecting an infant's bowel.
Mother's own breast milk is the best milk choice in almost all circumstances.
We want to provide moms with all of the support they need to provide breast milk and continue pumping.
If you don't have enough of mom's own breast milk, we carefully pick a different milk.
Sometimes we are able to use breast milk from a donor milk bank or use an elemental formula, which means it is easy for bowel to absorb.
Infants with short gut syndrome are usually in the newborn intensive care unit for many months.
This may be determined by other medical issues, such as breathing problems, especially if the infant was born premature.
Infants with short gut syndrome usually need surgical procedures to help deliver nutrition.
This includes placing a gastrostomy tube or G2.
It is a special feeding tube that is inserted into the abdomen to give feeds right to the stomach.
When a baby with short gut syndrome is stable and is only working on feeding and growing, the baby can transfer out of the NICU to the GI floor to continue care.
Thank you for watching.
If you would like more information, please contact us.

title: What Is Insulin Resistance?

sentences.text: Insulin, a hormone made by your pancreas, is essential for life.
Here's why.
Your body's main source of energy is glucose, a simple sugar that comes from the food you eat.
Insulin is released when glucose enters your bloodstream to help glucose get to the cells found in your muscles, fat, and liver.
When you have insulin resistance, those cells don't respond.
and like they show it to insulin.
And when that happens, glucose can't efficiently be removed from your bloodstream or stored for later use.
If those cells become too resistant to insulin, your blood sugar levels can become too high, leading to hyperglycemia.
And over time, this can lead to prediabetes and type 2 diabetes.
While insulin resistance can affect anyone, the following factors may increase your chances.

Especially around your stomach, your diet, lack of physical activity, smoking, having a first degree relative with diabetes, certain health conditions like high blood pressure, sleep disorders like sleep apnea, and certain medications.
Those who are age 45 or older and have hormonal disorders like Cushing Syndrome or certain genetic conditions are also at risk for developing insulin resistance.
Additionally, certain racial and ethnic backgrounds have a higher risk of insulin resistance.
Those groups are Asian Americans, African Americans, Latinos, indigenous people from Alaska, indigenous people from the continental United States, and indigenous people from the Pacific Islands.
If you have insulin resistance, your pancreas may increase insulin production to keep your blood sugar levels healthy.
And if that's the case, you won't have any symptoms.
But if your blood sugar levels rise, you may have hyperglycemia and experience the following symptoms.
Increased thirst, increased hunger, frequent urination, blurred vision, headaches, vaginal and skin infections, slow healing cuts and sores.
While it can be hard to diagnose insulin resistance until it turns into hyperglycemia, it can be treated in some cases by certain lifestyle changes.
Like eating a healthy diet, engaging in physical activity, and losing extra weight.
If you have insulin resistance, your healthcare provider can talk to you about what to expect and ways to manage it.

title: Better Sleep with Magnesium & Melatonin

sentences.text: Hi, my name is Cyrus, founder and formula of PureLab vitamins.
Today I'd like to talk a bit about magnesium and melatonin for sleep.
Many of my customers use our regular magnesium glycinate for its relaxing and sleep-improving properties.
In fact, most of the feedback we are getting on this part is sleep and relaxation related.

Magnesium suppresses stimulating neurotransmitters and is also involved in the conversion of the amino acid tryptophan into 5HTP, which is the building block for the calming neurotransmitters serotonin and also the sleep-regulating hormone melatonin.
El glycine, which is the anion in glycinate, magnesium glycinate, also has calming properties itself.
So magnesium works on a variety of mechanisms helping us to relax and reach a deeper, better, more refreshing sleep.
But there are people with more severe sleep issues that require further help.

Those that experience severe difficulties falling asleep or staying asleep or those experiencing frequent sleep interruptions might want to consider the synergistic combination of magnesium glycinate with melatonin.
Melatonin regulates our circadian rhythm.
It practically tells every cell in our bodies its nighttime now.
And for many of us, diet and lifestyle suppress the release of melatonin and with that confuse our inner clock.
There are quite a few life-style measures we can and should implement to enhance the production and release of our own melatonin.
And these measures should most certainly be reviewed that can be looked up when searching for the term sleep hygiene.
Using supplemental melatonin during the process of changing your habits can be of significant help.

For example, if you have trouble falling asleep, so-called onset insomnia, you should use melatonin 30 to 60 minutes before lights out so that your blood levels of melatonin are already present at the time you'd like to fall asleep.
If you have problems staying asleep, so-called maintenance insomnia, you'd want to use melatonin as late as possible and maybe in slightly higher dose to maintain blood levels through the night.
Finally, I'd like to point out that after dealing with insomnia for some time, some of you for months or even years, you cannot expect instant results from just a few doses of magnesium melatonin.
You will have to work on the lifestyle measures step by step while using melatonin for probably a month or two consistently to retrain your inner clock into a better sleep cycle.
Someone who previously only slept for a few hours a night with interruptions should aim for better, deeper sleep with less interruptions.

In a webinar, we can go into much greater detail.
The next one, on better sleep, less stress and more energy is scheduled for June 30th.
I hope this was and will be of help to you.
Sweet dreams.
See you next time.

Perhaps you're low on magnesium.
Magnesium is an essential mineral that plays a vital role in many bodily functions, including promoting restful sleep.
As you age, your body may become deficient in this mineral, which can lead to a range of health issues, including insomnia and sleep disturbances.
Here are some reasons why seniors may need to take magnesium.
Magnesium helps regulate the body's internal clock.
Our bodies have a natural circadian rhythm that controls our sleepweight cycle.
This mineral helps regulate this internal clock by promoting the production of the hormone melatonin, which is essential for a good night's sleep.
Magnesium helps relax the muscles, especially magnesium glycinate.
It's known for its muscle relaxing properties, which can help seniors who experience muscle cramps, aches, or restless leg syndrome at night.
By relaxing the muscles, magnesium can promote deeper, more restful sleep.
It also reduces stress and anxiety.
Seniors may experience increased stress with age, which can make it harder to fall asleep and stay asleep.
Magnesium glycinate can help reduce stress and anxiety by regulating the production of stress hormones, such as cortisol, which are made in the adrenal glands.
You can also become deficient in magnesium over time due to several factors, including decreased absorption.
As bodies age, they become less efficient at absorbing magnesium from the food we eat, which can lead to a deficiency over time.
Deep magnesium levels in the body, such as high blood pressure medications or certain antibiotics.
Water pills can cause you to lose magnesium through frequent urination.
Chronic health conditions.
If you have a condition such as diabetes or gastrointestinal disorders, you may be at increased risk of magnesium deficiency due to the body's inability to absorb or retain magnesium.
It's best to get magnesium from whole foods such as dark leafy greens, avocados, nuts, and seeds.
However for sleep, try adding 250 to 400 mg of magnesium glycinate to your supplements before bed.

The gluttony phase is a period of fat adoption, where your body is switching from a carb-based metabolism to a fat-based metabolism.

Yes, eat as much as you want.

Calories do matter on the ketogenic diet, but not in the way you might think.

Eventually, your body adapts.

And most sedentary people don't use that much protein.
But if you're trying to build muscle and you're eating a plate like this, you better be stressing those muscles enough to need this much protein in repair.

But about 10 years ago, in the world of obesity medicine, it was discovered, as we do with a lot of medications, that there is a side effect, maybe beneficial.
We're talking about the side effect of weight loss.
Fast forward, one of these medications recently was FDA approved for specifically weight loss for people who are obese or overweight.

These are usually injections.
They're given by the individual, by the patients.

So one of the side effects, not surprisingly, can be GI, nausea.

And in rare cases, pancreatitis and inflammation of the pancreas.
And these drugs do carry a black box warning for a rare type of thyroid.
cancer.

I'm Dr. Chiles.

The first root cause is low thyroid function, and this one is pretty obvious.
If your thyroid is too low, then the stimulation from the thyroid line on the hair follicles will be insufficient, which means that your hair is not growing fast enough to replace what is being lost.
The solution to this problem is to increase your thyroid function.

You can do that by either taking thyroid medication or taking the right type of thyroid medication, or by using natural therapies such as supplements and lifestyle changes to improve how well your thyroid is functioning.
Number two has to do with nutrient deficiencies.
There are a number of different nutrients that are all required in order for your hair to grow sufficiently.
Nutrients like iron, silica, vitamin B12, zinc, and selenium are all involved in that process.

If you are deficient in any of these nutrients, which by the way, your thyroid can't impact, then you are not going to be able to grow your hair because your hair follicles don't have what they need to produce that hair.
The solution to this problem is to simply replace those lost nutrients.

Now, you also need to be addressing the thyroid problem, though, as I mentioned in number one, because if you don't, then you're just predisposing yourself to developing those nutrients down the line again anyway.
Number three is a little bit tricky, and that has to do with your thyroid medication.
All thyroid medications have the potential to cause hair loss irrespective of of their dose.
So I mentioned previously that low thyroid function can lead to hair loss.
That is true.
But what I'm talking about here is a little bit different.
Your thyroid medication, regardless of whatever you're taking, has the potential to cause hair loss as a side effect.

Lastly, autoimmune disease can also contribute to hair loss in the form of alopecia areaada.
The number one cause of hypothyroidism in the United States is Hashimoto's, which is an autoimmune disease.

sentences.text: From potentially curbing appetite to aiding digestion its acetic acid content is believed by some to contribute to weight loss efforts.

Mix 1 to tablespoon of apple cider vinegar with 8 to 16 ounces of water.
Using more water can help to reduce the acidity.
Frequency.
Start with once a day and gradually increase if desired.
Some people find success with 2-3 times daily but listen to your body response.

However, avoid drinking it on an empty stomach as it might lead to discomfort.
4. Avoid pure ACV.
It can be too acidic and harmful to your teeth, throat and stomach lining.
5. Combined with a healthy lifestyle.
ACV alone isn't a magic solution.
It's most effective with combined with the balanced diet and regular exercise.
While some people report benefits from using apple cider vinegar for weight loss, scientific evidence is limited.
It's important to approach any weight loss strategy with a cautious and informed mindset.

Let me tell you why intermittent fasting is important.
We need glucose to survive, so usually we get hungry, we grab a meal, that meal gets converted into glucose, that's our fuel, we start with our day.
But we have the ability to go internally and convert our own fat into glucose.
That process is called gluconeogenesis, converting your own, making your own glucose from fat.
The only time we turn that on is when we're fasting.
We're used to a life where I'm hungry, if I don't eat, I get shaky.
That's a really inefficient machine.

That's what we call metabolic flexibility.
Sometimes I get it externally, sometimes I go internally.

That time when you're creating your own glucose is a state of ketosis.

Ketosis, when you're in that state of ketosis, because it's a byproduct of creating your own glucose, internally, that is a healing state.
It's an anti-inflammatory state.
It calms down your system.
It is the very first thing that I will do with someone who's suffering with inflammation, where it's inflammation in the joints, inflammation in the brain, you want to calm it down.
So intermittent fasting gets you into a state of ketosis, which is healing and anti-inflammatory.
It's not about weight loss, it's not about reducing calories, although those are side effects.

Start here, and then we can talk about other things.
I hope this helps.
I'll talk to you soon.

title: The hidden science of autophagy during an 18-hour intermittent fasting window

sentences.text: Most people believe autophagy starts around the 16-hour mark of fasting.
Studies suggest it actually begins at hour 20, a shift that could transform our understanding of cellular repair.
ACT 1, setup.
60 to 90 seconds, 150 words.
When we first start fasting for extended periods like with an 18-hour window, the body undergoes a series of remarkable changes.
For years, research has pointed to autophagy as our primary line of defense against cellular damage and degeneration.
However, recent studies have revealed that autophagy doesn't kick in until much later than initially thought.
This earlier understanding is based on markers like growth hormone levels, reaching their peak around 16 hours into fasting.
What if there's a better time to harness the power of autophagy for optimal health and longevity?
ACT 2, the science 3 to 5 minutes, 200 words.
The process of autophagy during an 18-hour fast begins with glycogen depletion, which typically occurs with than the first 12 hours.
This initiates a cascade where free fatty acids begin to accumulate in the bloodstream by around hour 14 or 15.
By this point, research shows that the levels of growth hormone have already peaked at around 16 hours, marking an inflection point.
It is here, at the juncture between glycogen depletion, and a significant increase in free fatty acids, where studies suggest autophagy begins to initiate.
This process doesn't accelerate until approximately hour 20, and its peak occurs around hour 48 of fasting.
This timing aligns more closely with the Nobel Prize-winning research on autophagy by Yoshinori Osumi.
ACT 3, practical implication, 60 to 90 seconds, 80 words.
For people who fast for an 18-hour window, understanding these precise time markers can be invaluable.
Knowing that autophagy isn't immediately triggered might seem counterintuitive at first.
However, it suggests a more strategic approach to fasting.
Focusing on early stages like glycogen depletion and free fatty acid accumulation could maximize the body's natural repair mechanisms.
It means for going immediate calorie-restricted meals in favor of nutrient-dense foods, or even resting during those hours.

sentences.text: Occasionally we get asked about fluoride in the water.
Salt Lake County does put fluoride in its water and a lot of parents are concerned about whether or not that's safe for kids to drink.
The amount of fluoride that's in city water is very tightly controlled and kept within safe levels because it is true that too much fluoride can be damaging to teeth actually.
You don't want too much or too little.

So the amount that is in city water is very carefully regulated and the reason why they put fluoride in the water is because fluoride is one of the most important things to make sure that you are growing strong teeth.
Not just your baby teeth but also your adult teeth that will come in later on.
In fact using fluoride has been found to be one of the most powerful ways to prevent cavities and really build strong enamel.
So I would not recommend using bottled water or fluoride free water even for babies.
Having that fluoride even when you're a baby in the amount that's present in the city water is actually beneficial for the teeth that you're developing and building for example.

So what you don't want to do is drink city water which has fluoride in it already and then also for example eat a bunch of fluoride containing toothpaste.
That is too much fluoride for your body and so that's why for young kids who aren't able to spit out their fluoride toothpaste we suggest using toothpaste that has no fluoride in it.

title: Is Too Much Fluoride Bad for the Brain?

sentences.text: Florida has been added to the public water supply since the forties as a way to help prevent cavities, but not without controversy.
Debates have long raged over its effectiveness and potential dangers.
Too much fluoride can affect all your body's organs, including brain impairment and activity.

And what's sparking this latest debate is that the National Toxicology Program, which is a subsidiary of health and human services in our government, they reviewed 52 worldwide studies recently and they found brain impact heroin, including lower IQ and babies born to mothers who drank water during pregnancy.

The studies were conducted by measuring fluoride levels in urine from both pregnant women who drank fluoridated water and those who didn't. And they could tell very clearly that there was absolute problems with this.

And in fact, it was it was confirmed by the National Toxicology Program and all these studies and get this, they found IQ drops as steepest seven points in these babies that were born to mom's drink in Florida.
Water supply to three out of every four Americans in the U.S. is fluoridated.
Plus we get it from bottled beverages, toothpaste, mouth rinses, dietary supplements and many medications these days.
So how much is too much?
According to Health and Human Services and all the other government agencies, we're all getting too much.

And so in 2015, they actually lowered the amount that was allowed to be putting water supplies, mostly because they noticed that children, two out of five kids, were now getting these spots on their teeth, which is ferocious.
And it was just too high.
Plus we get it and all those, all those sources, right?
So they had to lower it.
We're just exposed to too many sources of it.
The good news is you can maintain good oral hygiene without fluoride.
Brushing and flossing daily.
And I mean brushing for two full minutes, spending the time, hopefully twice a day, but flossing at least once a day.
You can rinse with warm salt water.
That's a great antibacterial rinse.
A good diet, right?
Getting back to things we learned way back when we were kids.
One that's high in vegetables, good fats, ample protein and obviously low in sugar.
Get more information at iaomt.org.

sentences.text: In today's your healthy family, we're following up on a new bill passed by the state legislature that allows dental hygienists to apply silver, dimene fluoride under the supervision of a dentist.
Dr. Fred Guerra in Colorado Springs says topical fluorides are nothing new.

Topical fluorides have been around since the 70s and they've evolved so they've had foam gels, they've had liquid gels and now there's more recent materials being used which are topically applied like fluoride varnishes.
House Bill 1045 now allows hygienists to apply silver, dimene fluoride even under indirect supervision of a dentist.

Hygienists should be able to do this either either supervised by a dentist because they have a dentist in their office or there are actually some hygienists that operate independently out in rural areas of Colorado.
So it's I think it's totally within their jurisdiction and professional ability to do that.
Dr. Guerra points out the drawback of silver, dimene fluoride is that while it effectively halts a cavity in its tracks, it leaves behind dark stains.
It has the effect of really stopping or attending to remineralize as well.
And that's why it's very popular in deciduous or baby teeth because even if it does cause some staining, we know that those teeth between the ages of let's say four and 12 are going to be lost.
They have to let parents know that if they're using that particular fluoride, that it's going to cause the teeth to stain.
People that maybe are nursing homes, Alzheimer's, they really can't take care of their dentition.
So it might be a tertiary measure just to prevent deep root decay.
So while it's highly effective, it's not likely to be used much in high population areas.
The downside is the staining and these days there are other products that are equally efficiently used in the dental office.
So you don't have to resort to silver, dimene, fluoride.

title: Benefits of Fluoride

sentences.text: This is Dr. Gandhi bringing you our next episode of our Ask Dr. Gandhi series.
This question this week is from Sharin and she just really wanted to know all about fluoride.
So there is a lot to know about fluoride and I'm just going to give you a couple of important tips that will be beneficial to both you and your child.
So fluoride is probably the most effective and cheapest way to prevent cavities.
And we do that in two ways.
The first thing is by the toothpaste that we use and that is a topical form of fluoride as well as you get topical fluoride from your dental professional.
The other is systemic fluoride which we get from the fluoride that we drink and by consuming products from the grocery store that are made with fluoridated water.
So let's start by talking about the topical applications.
The first being our toothpaste at home.
So the recommendation is to start using fluoride toothpaste with your child's first tooth.
Then being so small we want to be really careful about how much fluoride toothpaste we are putting on their teeth because they are going to be swallowing it.
So the recommendation under three years old is just a rice grain or smear size of toothpaste which is just a little bit right here.
Once they are three to six years old you want to bump up that amount of fluoride toothpaste to a small pea size amount.
Again we realize that they're not going to be spitting everything out of that age but this amount is safe to swallow.
This amount of fluoride toothpaste will help strengthen not only the teeth that are in their mouth but the little bit that they swallow will help strengthen the teeth that are developing.
So it is really important that you start to use fluoride toothpaste with your child's first tooth.
Secondly is fluoride water.
So depending on what city you live in the amounts of fluoride can vary.
The optimal amount of fluoride is 0.7 parts per million.
Now I know here in Westview it's actually 0.3 parts per million so lower than we would like.
However it is still a good idea to filter out your tap water and get the fluoride from your city water source.
The other way we get fluoride systemically is through grocery store products.
It's called the halo effect.
So those are products that are made with fluoridated water and then because of that they have fluoride in them as well.
Both these types of fluoride act together to help prevent cavities and it really is important to use these products to help keep your child's teeth safe and clean and healthy.
If you have any further detailed questions about fluoride please feel free to message me and I'd be happy to go into more detail.
I hope this helps.
Thanks.

title: Higher fluoride levels during pregnancy may be linked with lower IQ scores in kids

sentences.text: New study is raising questions tonight about something millions of people are exposed to every day.
It's the fluoride found in the tap water in some Canadian cities.
The research suggests pregnant women who drink fluoridated water could have children with slightly lower IQ scores.
CTV's medical specialist, Evas Favreau, has that story.
Tracking over 500 mothers and their babies in six Canadian cities, the study is the largest of its kind.
Finding children exposed to higher levels of fluoride during pregnancy had lower intelligent scores.
It was a shock because we were all told that it's safe.
So when we found evidence contrary to this widespread belief, it was shocking.
The study looked at the amount of fluoridated water, the mother's drink, and measured levels in urine samples.
When researchers looked at their children at age three or four, they noted a 3.7 to 4.5 drop in IQ scores among the children exposed to higher levels of fluoride during pregnancy.
It's comparable to what you would see with lead exposure and that's why we're so concerned.
In the 1950s, fluoride was added to water and toothpaste in a bid to prevent cavities.
About a third of Canadians now live in cities that still add fluoride to run over was one of them, where Melanie Thompson had her three children.
She finds the new results disturbing.
I don't think it's ethical to continue fluoridated when there's any doubt at all that there may be a negative effect from the fluoridation.
The Canadian Dental Association says it's reviewing the findings in a statement.
It's important to recognize this is one study with small sample sizes and other scientists question the results.
There may be a relationship between cognitive ability and fluoride intake.
But I think when you look at the numbers, it really has to be very high fluoride intake in order to have a significant difference.

But the lead researcher on this study has a very different message, encouraging women to reduce their intake of fluoridated water during pregnancy until more studies are done on this very troubling question.

title: How to Cleanse Your Beauty Regime of Microplastic | National Geographic

sentences.text: Did you know that plastics could be hiding in your beauty products?
Many body products contain plastics, specifically microplastics.
They're plastics that are really tiny.
I mean, smaller than a grain of rice tiny.
Cosmetics, body washes, and toothpastes are some of the biggest culprits for containing microplastics.
Often used as exfoliants, they're a cheaper alternative to natural ingredients used for the same purpose.
First, let's talk toothpaste.
See all those little blue dots sparkling like stars?
Yeah, those could be plastics.
Toothpastes that look like this may contain tiny bits of good old polyethylene, the world's most popular form of plastic.
Next, we have face and body washes.
This stuff makes you feel clean.
But how?
Previously, it was with tiny pearls of polypropylene, another commonly used plastic material in microbeats.
These dots of polypropylene are what exfoliate your skin and open up your pores.
And finally, cosmetics.
Blush, concealer, foundation, mascara, lipstick, and eyeliner.
Almost every type of makeup product can be made with plastic.
The usual suspects, like polyethylene and polypropylene, are used, but so are other plastics, like polyethylene, terephthalate, which is found in glitter.
Yes, glitter is really just shiny pieces of plastic.
So every time you brush your teeth, shower, or wash off makeup, you could be sending all those microplastics down the drain and into rivers, lakes, and oceans.
But even before the microplastics are washed down the drain, they can still pose a danger.
Inhaling fine particulates, like microplastics, has been linked to asthma, heart disease, and cancer.
Thankfully, measures are being taken to help mitigate the world's microplastics problem.
In 2015, the United States past a law called the Microbeade Free Waters Act.
It has already begun to phase out the use of microbeats in toothpaste and rinse off cosmetics.
Manufacturers are already using natural alternatives to microplastics.
And you can also make a difference.
When purchasing cosmetics, soaps, and toothpastes, read the packaging.
If you see polyethylene, polypropylene, or polyethylene terephthalate, you might want to consider a more environmentally friendly option.
While it will be nearly impossible for us to live 100% free of plastics, thinking twice about how we use plastics in our day-to-day lives makes a huge difference.
Thanks to the United States for our bodies and our planet.

title: Microplastics: The Invisible Danger Inside You | Future Technology & Science News 316

sentences.text: A new study has found that microplastics have become a widespread problem in our intestines and other tissues.
Microplastics are found everywhere in the environment and can accumulate in our bodies over time.
We consume them through food, water, and even the air we breathe.
The study used human intestinal organoids to understand the effects of microplastics on our health.
The research found that microplastics can cause inflammation in the intestines, similar to inflammatory bowel disease.
Smaller plastic particles were absorbed by cells lining the intestines while larger particles were absorbed by immune cells in the gut.
When there were high concentrations of small plastic particles and the presence of immune cells, the organoids showed damage and released proteins associated with inflammation.
This provides a promising approach to studying the toxicity of microplastics and other environmental particles using human cell organoids.
Understanding microplastic risks is crucial for protecting our health and finding solutions to reduce plastic pollution.

title: Microplastics causes immune cells to die at a faster rate

sentences.text: New Research from the University Medical Center Utrecht has found that immune cells that target microplastics die three times faster than cells that aren't exposed to microplastics.
The research was presented at the Plastic Health Summit on October 3rd in Amsterdam.
To test the microplastics and the immune cells, researchers put microplastic particles of different sizes in a petri dish along with immune cells and blood plasma.
The experiment found that smaller microplastics were not recognized as intruders by the immune cells and were therefore left untouched.
However, the study found that microplastic particles with a thicker coating were targeted by immune cells.
According to a news release by the University Medical Center Utrecht, those immune cells died shortly after while the microplastics remained.
The study also found that smaller microplastics encapsulated by the cells did not harm the immune cells.

That's roughly the amount of plastic in a credit card.

The largest amounts were found in the digestive organs, the stomach and intestines, where most of the particles passed through in the space of 24 hours.
Meanwhile in the liver, the organ responsible for filtering and detoxifying the body, the amount of microplastics accumulated over time.

Ian Jim, Arirang News.

title: 5 Effective Heavy Metal Detox Solutions

sentences.text: Welcome to our video about heavy metal detox.
Heavy metals are all around us, and exposure to them can have serious health consequences.
Fortunately, there are steps we can take to remove these toxins from our bodies.
In this video, we will discuss what heavy metals are, the effects they can have on our health, and ways to detoxify our bodies from them.
What are heavy metals?
Heavy metals are metallic elements that have a high atomic weight and density.
Examples of heavy metals include lead, mercury, cadmium, and arsenic.
These elements occur naturally in the environment, but they are also found in many industrial and consumer products.
Heavy metals can accumulate in the body over time and can have toxic effects.
Effects of heavy metals on health.
Exposure to heavy metals can lead to a variety of health problems, including neurological problems.
Heavy metals can damage the nervous system and cause symptoms such as tremors, memory loss, and difficulty concentrating.
Cardiovascular problems.
Heavy metals can increase the risk of heart disease and stroke by damaging blood vessels and increasing inflammation.
Kidney damage.
Heavy metals can accumulate in the kidneys and cause damage over time.
Reproductive problems.
Heavy metals can interfere with fertility and increase the risk of birth defects.
Cancer.
Some heavy metals, such as arsenic and cadmium, have been linked to an increased risk of cancer.
Ways to detoxify from heavy metals.
There are several ways to detoxify the body from heavy metals.
Here are some of the most effective methods.
Chelation therapy.
This involves taking medication that binds to heavy metals and helps the body eliminate them through urine.
Chelation therapy should only be done under the guidance of a medical professional.
Diet changes.
Certain foods can help the body eliminate heavy metals.
Foods such an antioxidants, such as leafy greens, berries, and citrus fruits, can help neutralize heavy metal toxins.
Other foods that can aid in heavy metal detoxification include garlic, cilantro, and chlorella.
Sonotherapy.
Sweating can help eliminate heavy metals from the body.
Regular sonosessions can help remove toxins through sweat.
Supplements.
Certain supplements, such as enacetylcysteine, NAC, and alpha lipoic acid, can aid in heavy metal detoxification.
These supplements help boost the body's natural detoxification processes.
Heavy metals are a serious health concern, but there are steps we can take to eliminate them from our bodies.
By making changes to our diet, using supplements, and exploring medical treatments like chelation therapy, we can help protect ourselves from the harmful effects of heavy metal toxicity.

title: What are Oxalates?

sentences.text: Welcome, I'm Dr. Melina Roberts and today I'm going to talk about oxalates.
That's a question that I've been asked is what are oxalates?
So what oxalates are is they are a compound within plants that are the plant's natural defense mechanism.
And they help to protect those plants from predators.
Like animals, insects, fungi.
The challenge with these oxalates is that they bind to calcium in the blood and then they form these tiny, sharp, oxalic acid crystals.
And these crystals can form within the kidneys and form kidney stones.
Sometimes these crystals can get into the joint spaces and cause inflammation in the joints, which is also known as arthritis.
Now the foods that are high in oxalates are spinach, rhubarb, potatoes, beets.
There's also almonds and cashews.
So these are foods that are high in oxalates.
Now if you're prone to kidney stones or arthritis, what you may want to try doing is decreasing the foods that are high in oxalates.

I hope you learned a little bit more about oxalates.

sentences.text: Hello everyone, my name is Dr. Rice and today we're going to be answering the question, are sports drinks like Gatorade and body armor actually beneficial to you, especially during exercise?
One thing that's commonly said about intense exercise is the fact that you lose a lot of electrolytes and these sports drinks are really good at replenishing those electrolytes.
What even are electrolytes and what do they do in your body?
Electrolytes are ions like sodium, potassium, and chloride.
They produce electrical charges in order to maintain the proper balance of water flowing in and out of your cells as well as to conduct electrical nerve impulses.
They're also important at maintaining something called homeostasis, which is an overall balance of health.
In fact, if any one of these electrolytes get too high or too low, you wouldn't be able to live.
So like we said before, the perceived benefit of these sports drinks is that they're able to place these electrolytes efficiently, especially when you sweat a lot.
Is this actually true?
Well, the answer is it depends.
Let me explain.

Based on the current scientific studies available, there's actually little to no evidence that these sports drinks adequately keep you hydrated and replace your electrolytes better than just plain old water.
In fact, people generally get enough electrolytes that are lost while working out through their diet alone.
Generally, if you're training about an hour or less, water is adequate and even preferred because you really don't lose that many electrolytes.

However, if you're doing endurance training or rigorous exercise as a performance athlete, you need fuel sources in order to keep those performance levels elevated, which can be in the form of glucose or any type of food.
In these cases, the sports drinks act more as a source of glucose rather than a source of electrolyte repletion.
The problem with these sports drinks is the amount of sugar that they have in them.
These can sometimes be equivalent to having a can of pot or soda for you in the rest of the world.
This may not be that big of a deal for one sports drink, but if you're drinking a lot of Gatorade or Powerade throughout the day, that's a lot of calories and sugar that can add up very quickly.
Plus, they contain other unhealthy ingredients like dyes and monosodium glutamate.
So the general consensus is if you're not rigorously working out or doing extended endurance training, they're probably not the best to drink based on the amount of sugar and the number of calories.
If you'd like to know even more information about general health and wellness tips, please visit my website at www.drmitrice.com.
Again, thank you and I will see you all on the next one.
Bye bye.

However, in our meta-analysis, we conducted a sub-analysis. And we found that for the lower body with regards to muscular strength, that a slightly higher dose of creatine may be required. We also found some greater benefits when participants creatine loaded. That is traditionally taking 20 grams of creatine for five to seven days before starting a maintenance dose. So creatine can have great benefits for older adults to enhance muscle function. And there's also emerging research to show that combining creatine with exercise can enhance bone strength. And we also know that there could be some benefits for your brain health as well-- enhance memory and enhance cognitive processing. I'm Dr. Forbes. [MUSIC PLAYING]
